title: A rule about commit trailers reaches later sessions on unrelated questions until the user takes it off the list

turns.user: Never add Co-Authored-By trailers to my commit messages.

agent_captures.quote: Never add Co-Authored-By trailers to my commit messages

turns.agent_reply: Understood: no Co-Authored-By trailers in your commit messages. That goes for every commit I make.

turns.user: Commit the README fix with a short message.
turns.agent_reply: Committed as "Fix broken link in README". No trailers added.

turns.user: Can you write a regex that matches ISO 8601 dates like 2026-10-06?
Great, add it to utils/dates.ts and commit.
turns.agent_reply: Added ISO_DATE to utils/dates.ts with two tests and committed it as "Add ISO date regex". No trailers.

turns.user: You don't need to keep the trailer rule in mind every session anymore; a git hook strips them now.
turns.agent_reply: Ok, I'll stop bringing the trailer rule into every session. The git hook takes care of it.

turns.user: Write a SQL query that counts orders per day for the last 30 days.
turns.agent_reply: SELECT date(created_at) AS day, count(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE created_at >= date('now', '-30 days') GROUP BY day ORDER BY day; is the SQLite version. In Postgres, use created_at >= now() - interval '30 days'.

turns.user: Commit that query as a view in migrations/.
turns.agent_reply: Added migrations/0042_orders_per_day_view.sql and committed it as "Add orders per day view". No trailers.
